updates.summary: Reference the contract that witnesses a named piece of work finding its procedure, bind the observed labels to the operations that emit them, and make any report or summary of discovery firing answer to it.
updates.reason: A claim that discovery fired must be backed by a witness contract, not by an invocation log read by hand.

updates.summary: Replace the generated poa invoke bindings with dotdiw's real command line, bind every operation to one inline body in dotdiw through promise_bindings.py, declare beads and git as the products dotdiw calls and name the calls, correct the kinds the step-id heuristic got wrong, and give the request and response types the fields the bodies use.
updates.reason: Until the bindings are real, POA checks the artifacts against each other and never against the program. These are the facts that let it check the program.

updates.summary: Invoke every operation through one door generated from the IDL into dotdiw: the request held to its type on the way in, the response to its own on the way out, the witness log appended and the terminal fed from the typed response, with the request and response types made true to what the bodies use. Migration plan: none; nothing a worker sees changes, and seventeen commands print the same bytes as before.
updates.reason: A body bound to the IDL in name only read fields its type never declared, printed what no response carried and wrote the witness log itself, and nothing noticed. Through one door the types are the contract, every transport runs the same bodies, and the tests hold the program to the IDL from its source.

updates.summary: Put the tracker behind a door of its own: the ten operations of a tracker interface, with typed requests and responses, generated into dotdiw as a second table and answered by an adapter chosen per request, else per workspace, else the shipped default, with one implementation binding per adapter for each. Two adapters ship: local, a sqlite store under the workspace's keyed directory and the default for a new adoption, and beads, the tracker of every version before, kept to its bytes; a third, for Jira Cloud, is loaded by name from the home and proved against a stub. Four operations list, choose, check and migrate. Migration plan: a workspace adopted by an earlier version is pinned to beads by its first command and told so once; nothing a worker who chose nothing sees changes, and under beads the same twenty commands print the same bytes; dotdiw tracker migrate moves a workspace between adapters, ids kept where the target accepts them and mapped in a record under the workspace where it does not, the source never written.
updates.reason: Eight bodies reached one tracker by name through two runners and a stream rewrite, and the IDL named the product and its calls without an interface a second tracker could answer. Behind a door of its own the interface is the record: every adapter is held to the same types by the door and to the same scenario by the conformance suite, the bodies cross nowhere but the door, and a worker can choose a tracker, or none, without dotdiw changing.

updates.summary: A module is looked for in the home directory and then in share/dotdiw/trackers beside the tool; it says which interface it was written for, and any other is refused by name when it loads; dotdiw tracker check takes a file by path; dotdiw tracker new writes the file to start from, generated from the interface. Two operations ship a tracker. The tap's formula no longer installs beads. Migration plan: a module written for 0.6.0 declares no interface and is read as interface 1; a checkout on beads goes on working while the binary is on the machine, and is told the one command when it is not.
updates.reason: A tracker could only be copied by hand into the home directory, which a package manager cannot write to, and nothing said which interface a module was written for.

reportBindings.storyClaim: Work was named and the procedure that applies surfaced for it before it began.

storySummaryBindings.storyClaim: What happened to a piece of named work, from create to the last step closed.

types.name: HeldFormula
types.description: A formula the project holds, as read from its committed file: what ListFormulas lists, MatchFormulas surfaces and the witness records.

fields.name: formulaRef
fields.summary: The formula's id, as its file declares it; the file's name when it declares none.

fields.name: name
fields.summary: The file's name without its extensions, which is what MatchFormulas prints.

fields.name: description
fields.summary: The description as written in the file.

fields.name: path
fields.summary: The repository-relative path of the file.

fields.name: examples
fields.summary: The example titles the file declares, in its order.

types.name: FormulaExample
types.description: One example title of one formula, named so that the conventions check can take it out of the index while that formula is searched for.

fields.name: formulaRef
fields.summary: The formula whose example it is.

fields.name: example
fields.summary: The example title, as the file declares it.

types.name: ConventionProblem
types.description: One problem DescribeAndCheck found: where it is, what is wrong, and which convention it breaks.

fields.name: kind
fields.summary: convention: an instruction file that does not say where work starts, or the tracker's directory tracked in git. formula: a formula that is uncommitted, outside the repository, too short to name a situation, still a scaffold, short of examples, or not retrieved by one of its examples.

fields.name: where
fields.summary: The file, repository-relative; the absolute path of a formula outside the repository.

fields.name: what
fields.summary: What is wrong with it, and the command that puts it right when there is one.

types.name: HandmadeProcedure
types.description: A procedure carried out in the tracker and never declared: a parent that is not a molecule, with ordered children, that no formula reaches.

fields.name: workRef
fields.summary: The parent's id, which formula new --from turns into steps.

fields.name: title
fields.summary: The parent's title, which becomes the formula's.

fields.name: stepCount
fields.summary: How many ordered children it has.

types.name: TrackerItem
types.description: One item of the tracker as an adapter returns it: what every tracker operation reads and writes, whichever adapter answers.

fields.name: id
fields.summary: The adapter's id for the item; opaque to dotdiw, prefixed where the adapter honours the workspace prefix.

fields.name: title
fields.summary: The title as given.

fields.name: kind
fields.summary: task, epic, chore or what the adapter calls them; task when unsaid.

fields.name: status
fields.summary: open, in_progress, blocked or closed.

fields.name: priority
fields.summary: 0 is highest; 2 when unsaid.

fields.name: parent
fields.summary: The parent's id, when the item is a child.

fields.name: reason
fields.summary: Why it was closed, when it was.

fields.name: needs
fields.summary: Ids of the items this one needs closed first.

fields.name: createdAt
fields.summary: When it was made, as the adapter states it.

fields.name: updatedAt
fields.summary: When it last changed, as the adapter states it.

types.name: TrackerEdge
types.description: A need between two items: the first cannot close while the second is open.

fields.name: id
fields.summary: The item that needs.

fields.name: needs
fields.summary: The item it needs closed first.

types.name: TrackerStep
types.description: One step of a formula as handed to the tracker to pour: its id within the formula, its title and the step ids it needs.

fields.name: id
fields.summary: The step's id in the formula.

fields.name: title
fields.summary: The step's title.

fields.name: needs
fields.summary: Step ids this one needs, by the formula.

types.name: TrackerInfo
types.description: What an adapter says of itself: its name and version, where it came from, and what it can do.

fields.name: name
fields.summary: The registered name: local, beads, or the name it was loaded under.

fields.name: version
fields.summary: The adapter's own version, or the product's behind it.

fields.name: interface
fields.summary: The tracker interface it was written for; a module that says nothing was written for interface 1.

fields.name: origin
fields.summary: Inside dotdiw, or loaded by name from the home directory or share/dotdiw/trackers.

fields.name: source
fields.summary: The file it was loaded from, when loaded.

fields.name: nativeNeeds
fields.summary: Whether the product behind it holds needs itself, or the adapter keeps them in a sidecar.

fields.name: checkTarget
fields.summary: Where tracker check may create and close items: a project, a board, a throwaway store; absent, the check refuses to run.

fields.name: extras
fields.summary: What the adapter offers beyond the interface, by name; forward, for the beads adapter's pass-through.

types.name: TrackerCheckResult
types.description: One operation of the conformance scenario as it ran against an adapter.

fields.name: operation
fields.summary: The operation id.

fields.name: status
fields.summary: Whether the adapter answered as the interface says.

fields.name: detail
fields.summary: What failed, when it did.
